newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker offers bill to curb credit card fees.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker offers bill to curb credit card fees.

text.p: With a growing number of consumers struggling under a heavy load of credit card debt, Representative Joe Kennedy offered legislation on Thursday to curtail fees charged by credit card companies.
"One of the alarming trends in our country is the explosive growth in consumer debt and personal bankruptcies," the Massachusetts Democrat told a news briefing.
Revolving credit debt has grown by 33 percent to $400 billion in the past two years, while delinquent credit card payments have risen by 50 percent over the same period, Kennedy noted.
"The evidence is strong that this growth in credit card debt and credit card delinquencies has come about due to the tactics of credit card companies," he added.

The proposed legislation would require better disclosure of interest rates and short-term "teaser" rates. The bill also would require card issuers to freeze the rate and terms on cancelled cards and would prohibit over-limit fees if the issuer had approved the charge.

Consumer advocates endorsed the legislation. "The credit card marketplace is not fair to consumers," said Ed Mierzwinski of the U.S. Public Interest Research Group. "Congressman Kennedy's legislation will go a long way in leveling the playing field for consumers and will prohibit unfair and deceptive credit card practices."
The Consumer Federation of America released a survey of consumers that showed strong support for many of the provisions in the Kennedy bill.

About 73 percent of those surveyed said card issuers are not adequately disclosing so-called teaser rates and 75 percent agreed cardholders should be allowed to cancel and pay off balances at the existing rate.
Credit card companies have generally opposed government restrictions on charge card rates and policies.
